summary: Colorectal adenocarcinoma rules for crypt/gland continuity, malignant gland interfaces, cribriform units, mucin, budding, desmoplasia, and bowel-wall tissues.

rules.claim: Do not partially cut, fuse, or erase a recognizable normal crypt during a generic tumor or stroma burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A dedicated normal-to-neoplastic transformation primitive with a complete gland-level contract.
counterexamples: Replacing one wall of a normal crypt with tumor.
Bridging two normal crypts through the lamina propria.
expected_morphology: Normal crypt contour, lumen, and local alignment remain coherent.
forbidden_morphology: Abrupt crypt notch, half-crypt deletion, crypt fusion, or isolated epithelial remnants.
known_limitations: Tangentially sectioned crypts require broader context and may be ambiguous.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: A local burden edit must not create an abrupt indentation, partial epithelial cut, narrow neck, or lumen loss in an otherwise coherent gland.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: Poorly differentiated/discohesive carcinoma without recognizable gland formation must use the budding/discohesive rule.
counterexamples: A deep narrow retreat from a short interface into a large malignant gland.
An expansion that closes the gland lumen.
A bridge that merges neighboring glands.
expected_morphology: Smooth continuous epithelial contour with preserved lumen and gland-object identity.
forbidden_morphology: Deep notch, V-shaped cut, jagged stair-step, gland split/merge, narrow neck, or hole filling.
known_limitations: Native gland instances are required to distinguish touching glands reliably.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Treat a cribriform tumor as a coherent epithelial unit with multiple internal luminal spaces; do not fill the spaces or carve a local slot through the unit.
rules.required_observation: Identify the external outline and all visible internal luminal spaces before generating candidates.
exceptions: True intraglandular necrosis/debris is not equivalent to a luminal space and requires explicit distinction.
counterexamples: Morphological closing that solidifies a sieve-like gland.
Tumor decrease that opens a slit from one internal lumen to the exterior.
expected_morphology: External and internal cribriform contours remain mutually coherent.
forbidden_morphology: Luminal-space filling, space-to-exterior cuts, unit bisection, or solidification.
known_limitations: Cribriform architecture may be absent from coarse gland annotations.

rules.claim: Do not treat mucin pools, lumina, or dirty necrotic debris as editable stroma or generic background.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A dedicated mucinous or necrosis primitive with profile support.
counterexamples: Growing a gland across a mucin lake because the profile maps non-gland complement to Stroma.
Shrinking tumor into dirty necrosis and labeling it fibrous stroma.
expected_morphology: Mucin/lumen/debris relationships to tumor epithelium remain unchanged in a burden-only edit.
forbidden_morphology: Mucin-pool filling, lumen-to-stroma conversion, or necrosis-to-stroma substitution.
known_limitations: Profiles such as transformed GLaS do not separately encode mucin, lumen, or necrosis.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Do not convert sparse buds or poorly cohesive invasive cells into a filled solid tumor region or connect them by broad morphological closing.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A coarse annotation protocol may outline an aggregate reviewed compartment, but local growth must still be H&E-compatible.
counterexamples: Taking a convex hull around multiple buds.
Filling desmoplastic stroma between isolated cell clusters.
expected_morphology: Discohesive spacing and infiltrative front remain visible and compatible with the source component.
forbidden_morphology: Bulk solidification, long bridges between buds, or invented gland formation.
known_limitations: Tumor budding assessment is scale- and field-selection-dependent.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Select a broad existing tumor-desmoplastic-stroma interface and spread area along it before increasing penetration depth.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: If no broad compatible interface exists, abstain rather than force the requested area.
counterexamples: Meeting a 19% change through one narrow inward wedge.
Calling smooth muscle or non-gland complement desmoplastic stroma without H&E support.
expected_morphology: Shallow distributed displacement along a visually compatible tumor-stroma front.
forbidden_morphology: Deep slots, angular bites, remote regions, or expansion through nonstromal compartments.
known_limitations: Depth/span thresholds require scale- and profile-specific calibration.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Do not use muscularis mucosae, muscularis propria, submucosa, nerve, or vessel as generic stroma in a local burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Identify bowel-wall compartment, smooth-muscle bundle orientation, vessels, and nerves at the proposed interface.
exceptions: A dedicated invasion-depth primitive with bowel-wall compartment labels and review.
counterexamples: Expanding tumor through a muscular layer because it is labeled Stroma.
Erasing a nerve or vessel to smooth the tumor boundary.
expected_morphology: Unrequested bowel-wall structures remain intact and the edit stays on the selected tissue interface.
forbidden_morphology: Cross-compartment growth, muscle-bundle bisection, vessel/nerve loss, or false invasion-depth change.
known_limitations: Most patch-level datasets do not explicitly label bowel-wall compartments.
